recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Revisit only if OO opens a new issue for broader nutrition-domain guidance, such as water/value-set interpretation or chain-of-custody beyond the bounded FHIR-46702/FHIR-48640 decisions.
issue_request: FHIR-46702 was an Applied/Persuasive with Modification R6 request for NutritionProduct to address human milk and link to BiologicallyDerivedProduct-style boundary guidance, with additional questions about whether breast milk source/manufacturer and provenance could be represented.
initial_application: The application occurred through related OO tickets and follow-up commits rather than a standalone FHIR-46702-only source commit. FHIR-46613 added NutritionProduct-side boundary text; FHIR-46604 added reciprocal BiologicallyDerivedProduct-side text; d0f9f0cb921ca73af9137792711cb1d73df8e5c1 explicitly lists FHIR-46702 while removing an overly narrow NutritionProduct scope phrase and applying the related FHIR-48640 manufacturer/traceability updates; 9c85a7b7d0fb8e2043768ba811c76eb7d5db49a6 later consolidated the boundary text while preserving the donated human milk guidance.
additional_context: FHIR-46702's resolution explicitly points boundary concerns to FHIR-46613/FHIR-46604 and traceability/manufacturer concerns to FHIR-48640. FHIR-48640 already has a no-change audit commit on the combined branch, so duplicating that issue was avoided. OO Confluence minutes corroborate the FHIR-46702 vote and the linked FHIR-48640 RelatedPerson/biologicalSourceEvent discussion; Zulip searches found no conflicting discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. NutritionProduct and BiologicallyDerivedProduct are active in source/fhir.ini; the current NutritionProduct and BiologicallyDerivedProduct introductions link the resource pair, distinguish dietary administration from transplant/infusion/therapeutic administration/injection, and explicitly call out donated human milk ambiguity. NutritionProduct.manufacturer already references Organization and RelatedPerson, and NutritionProduct.instance.biologicalSourceEvent remains the traceability hook.
